title: Effective Ionic Valence and Local Magnetic Moment in Kagome Superconductors
authors: Ruoshi Jiang, Zi-Jian Lang, Yuzki Oey, Andrea Capa Salinas, Stephen D. Wilson, Yongwei Li, Ilya Shipulin, Yiwen Zhang, Deng Hu, Zhiwei Wang, Hans-Henning Klauss, Zurab Guguchia, Vadim Grinenko, Wei Ku
abstract: In order to understand the unexpected similarity and the correlated behavior in kagome superconductor families AV$_3$Sb$_5$ (A = K, Rb, Cs) and ATi$_3$Bi$_5$ (A = Rb, Cs), we investigate the Hartree-scale local electronic structure of these systems. Our result indicates that V and Ti ions are both of 2+ valence such that the corresponding itinerant carrier densities are similar, and the difference in electron count is instead reflected in their quantum fluctuating ionic magnetic moments. However, due to the frustrated lattice geometry of these materials, such local moments are difficult to experimentally observe via standard probes. For verification, we systematically introduce nonmagnetic Sn impurities to locally relieve the geometric frustration and experimentally demonstrate the existence of well-defined local magnetic moments via magnetic susceptibility and muon spin rotation or relaxation ($μ$SR) measurements. All experiments discover a systematic increase of magnetic susceptibility upon increasing nonmagnetic impurity level. Our discovered ionic moments suggest a paradigm shift from the existing itinerant carrier-only picture to one incorporating strong correlation from local ionic spins. The associated interatomic and local-itinerant correlations offer a solid ground for the emergence of the observed rich correlated behavior in this new family of superconducting materials.
summary: This work investigates the correlated behavior in Kagome superconductors by proposing that local ionic magnetic moments, rather than just itinerant carriers, are crucial. Theoretical calculations predict these moments, and experimental doping with Sn impurities successfully confirms their existence via magnetic measurements. This suggests a major revision to existing models of superconductivity in these materials.
main_problem: The paper aims to resolve the discrepancy in understanding the correlated behavior of Kagome superconductors ($	ext{AV}_3	ext{Sb}_5$ and $	ext{ATi}_3	ext{Bi}_5$) by investigating the role of local ionic magnetic moments.
main_result: The study suggests a paradigm shift from purely itinerant carrier descriptions to one that must incorporate strong correlations arising from local ionic spins, which were experimentally confirmed via Sn-doping.
method: The approach combines Hartree-scale electronic structure calculations to model local moments with experimental measurements (magnetic susceptibility and $\mu	ext{SR}$) on doped samples.
model_or_system: The physical systems are Kagome lattice superconductors, specifically $	ext{AV}_3	ext{Sb}_5$ and $	ext{ATi}_3	ext{Bi}_5$. The theoretical modeling focuses on capturing short-range physics and local orbital-specific density of states.
key_observables: Local magnetic moments, magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$), spin relaxation rates ($\mu	ext{SR}$), and local electronic valence states.
important_parameters: The doping concentration ($x$) of nonmagnetic Sn impurities, which is used to locally relieve geometric frustration.
main_assumptions: The initial theoretical calculations are performed in a non-collinear Curie-paramagnetic phase to avoid assuming long-range magnetic order.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the local atomic orbital-specific DOS for the superconducting compounds, the mechanism by which Sn impurities relieve geometric frustration, and the temperature dependence of magnetic susceptibility showing Curie-Weiss behavior proportional to doping.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the theoretical framework using Hartree-scale calculations to predict local moments, then using Sn-doping to experimentally verify the existence of these moments, and finally concluding with the necessity of incorporating local spin correlations into the superconducting picture.
why_interesting: The emphasis on local moments and strong correlations in a geometrically frustrated superconducting lattice is highly relevant to understanding exotic quantum states in strongly correlated electron systems.
